subject.title: feat(plugin-sdk): generic outbound delivery-report seam; WhatsApp native auto-reply reports provider-accepted sends

question: Should OpenClaw accept `openclaw/plugin-sdk/outbound-delivery-report` as the public channel-owned way to report self-delivered outbound messages into canonical sent hooks?
rationale: This adds a release-facing Plugin SDK contract and exactly-once/idempotency semantics; automation can review the implementation, but maintainers must own the API shape before external plugins depend on it.

options.title: Accept seam after proof
options.body: Require redacted WhatsApp/runtime proof, resolve the dirty branch, and explicitly approve this narrow public API shape before merging.

options.title: Revise API shape first
options.body: Keep the PR open but request maintainer-directed naming or payload-contract changes before proof and final review.

options.title: Pause the branch
options.body: If maintainers are not ready to own a generic SDK reporting contract, keep the linked issue as the design point and pause or close this PR.

recommendation.title: Accept seam after proof
recommendation.body: Require redacted WhatsApp/runtime proof, resolve the dirty branch, and explicitly approve this narrow public API shape before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest routing candidate from merged outbound hook and sibling sent-hook history, and this decision spans core, Plugin SDK, and bundled channel boundaries.
